hook: Six men on one upside down boat, two miles out.
narration: Six men were sitting on an upside down boat, two miles off the mouth of the Columbia River.
It was about ten in the morning on May twenty ninth, two thousand nine.
The Coast Guard found them with Rescue 21, a radio system that takes a bearing on a distress call and points crews to where it came from.
A forty seven foot motor lifeboat from Station Cape Disappointment pulled up alongside the hull.
Overhead, a helicopter crew from Air Station Astoria lowered a rescue swimmer into the water.
One by one, the men came off the hull and onto the lifeboat.
outcome: All six men were rescued off their capsized boat by the lifeboat and helicopter crews.

location_card.place: Mouth of the Columbia River, Washington

title: Six men on an upside down boat
description:
A 47-foot motor lifeboat crew from Coast Guard Station Cape Disappointment and an MH-60J helicopter crew from Air Station Astoria rescue six men from their capsized boat two miles from the mouth of the Columbia River on May 29, 2009.

facts.claim: Six men rescued off a capsized vessel two miles from the Columbia River mouth, about 10 a.m. May 29, 2009, by a 47-foot lifeboat from Cape Disappointment and an Astoria helicopter
facts.source_quote: six men are rescued off their capsized vessel by a 47-motor lifeboat crew from Station Cape Disappointment, Wash., and an MH-60J rescue helicopter crew from Group/Air Station Astoria, Ore., two miles from the mouth of the Columbia River around 10 a.m. Friday, May 29, 2009.
The vessel was located with the help of the Coast Guard's Rescue 21 communication system.
